What disqualifies a protein bar from being gluten free

We check the Gluten Free (Y/N) label on file for every bar, then cross-check ingredient lists ourselves for wheat and barley or malt, the two gluten sources that show up by name in our data. 835 of 1,308 bars, about 64%, carry a gluten free label. The other 473, about 36%, don't.

Wheat is the most common named culprit at 62 bars (4.7% of the full database), followed by barley or malt at 30 bars (2.3%). The remaining 395 bars, 30.2% of the full database, show no wheat or barley in their own ingredient list at all. They just aren't labeled gluten free, which is a different claim from actually containing gluten.

Wheat
62 bars4.7%
The most common named gluten source, usually as wheat flour, a wheat-based crisp, or a graham/cookie piece mixed into the bar.
Found in: Anabar, Barebells, Built, Einstein
and 12 moreHide, FITCRUNCH, Fields Good, Gatorade, House of Yes, Lenny & Larry's, MET-Rx, MyProtein, Nature Valley, Neoh, NuGo, Power Crunch, Wonderslim
Barley / Malt
30 bars2.3%
Shows up as barley malt extract or malt syrup, usually a flavoring or sweetener rather than a structural ingredient.
Found in: Anabar, Built, CLIF Bar, Fields Good
and 3 moreHide, Jambar, Power Crunch, Wonderslim
Not labeled gluten free
395 bars30.2%
No wheat or barley shows up anywhere in the ingredient list we can find, but the brand hasn't labeled or certified the bar gluten free either. That is a labeling gap, not proof the bar contains gluten.

What we found screening 1,308 bars

30.2%
of all protein bars show no wheat or barley, yet still aren't labeled gluten free
395 of the 1,308 bars we track have no wheat or barley anywhere in their own ingredient list, but the brand hasn't labeled or certified them gluten free. Not being labeled gluten free is not the same as containing gluten.
Wheat is the clearest single gluten source.
62 bars (4.7% of the database) name wheat directly, more than double the barley/malt count.
CLIF Bar is not a gluten free brand.
None of CLIF Bar's 14 flavors carry a gluten free label. 14 list barley or malt as an ingredient. 5 carry a "may contain wheat" warning on top of that.
116 brands are gluten free across their entire lineup.
Led by Larabar (29), think! (22), Bobo's (21), and Perfect Bar (19), these brands never reach for wheat or barley in the first place, rather than swapping it out flavor by flavor.
Gluten free bars grade slightly better than the database average.
61.0% of gluten free bars grade A or B, against 54.9% database-wide.
Gluten free bars average less protein, about the same fiber.
Gluten free bars average 12.1g of protein against a database-wide average of 13.3g, and 5.0g of fiber vs. 5.0g.
Lenny & Larry's splits closer to even than any other large lineup.
7 of the 17 Lenny & Larry's flavors are gluten free, the rest are not.

  • Every ingredient is scored individually against a canonical database, not just flagged good or bad
  • Position in the ingredient list matters, earlier ingredients carry more weight
  • Each bar's total becomes a single letter grade, A through F

Frequently asked questions

We use the Gluten Free (Y/N) label on file for each bar. 835 of the 1,308 bars we track carry that label. We also cross-check ingredient lists ourselves for wheat and barley or malt, the two named gluten sources that show up most in the data.
835 of the 1,308 bars we track are labeled gluten free, spanning 132 brands. 182 of those 835 bars grade A for ingredient quality.
Not by label. None of CLIF Bar's 14 flavors carry a gluten free label. 14 list barley or malt as an ingredient. 5 carry a "may contain wheat" warning on top of that. If you need to avoid gluten, look elsewhere.
Yes. All 29 Larabar flavors we track are labeled gluten free. Larabar builds its bars around dates, nuts, and fruit rather than a wheat-based binder or crisp.
Wheat. It shows up by name in 62 of the 1,308 bars we track, more than double the count for barley or malt. Most other non-gluten-free bars simply aren't labeled, without a named gluten ingredient we can find.
Not necessarily. 395 of the 473 bars that don't carry our gluten free label show no wheat or barley anywhere in their own ingredient list. The brand just hasn't labeled or certified the bar, which is a different claim from it containing gluten.
Yes. Lenny & Larry's splits closest to even of any large lineup we checked: 7 of 17 flavors are gluten free. Always check the specific flavor, not just the brand.
835 bars across 132 brands carry a gluten free label, led by brands like Larabar and think! that qualify across their entire lineup. The full ranked list is in the table below, sorted by ingredient quality.
473 of the 1,308 bars we track don't carry a gluten free label. Wheat is the most common named reason, followed by barley or malt. Most of the remaining bars simply haven't been labeled, without an identifiable gluten ingredient in the list.
No. Gluten free bars in our database grade A or B at a slightly higher rate than the database as a whole (61.0% vs. 54.9%). What they give up on average is protein: gluten free bars average 12.1g against a database-wide average of 13.3g.
We update the database whenever new bars are added or a brand reformulates. Manufacturers do change their ingredient lists over time, so always confirm against the packaging in front of you. This page reflects the database as of 2026-09-24.
